correctness.rationale: PASS: The positive defect B=I−G*G yields the spectral estimate epsilon||Q_epsilon x||²<=1−||Gx||². This forces p_G(Q_epsilon)=0. Under universal equality every Q_epsilon is compact, hence finite rank, making B norm-compact by truncation; a rank-one projection onto a zero-defect vector rules out ker B. Conversely compactness and injectivity give finite-rank Q_epsilon and strongly null P_epsilon; near-G vectors have vanishing Q_epsilon norm, and all unit vectors in ran P_epsilon are near-G norming. This proves p_G(T)=lim||TP_epsilon||. Removing TQ_epsilon is a finite-rank approximation and KP_epsilon→0 for each compact K, proving equality with essential norm in both directions. The separability corollary uses dense range of compact injective B and an explicit diagonal example. These steps verify all real/complex, arbitrary-dimensional quantifiers and endpoint restrictions.

value.rationale: PASS: The same recently studied G-relative seminorm can be exactly the Calkin quotient norm rather than an ordinary operator norm. The theorem classifies precisely which norm-one G realize that quotient for every bounded operator, identifies the kernel and an exact spectral formula, and shows a separability boundary. The spectral compactness and injectivity tests are structurally forced by the quotient ideal; this is a natural general operator-ideal characterization, not a computation for an arbitrary parameter slice.
